pasos: 1. Instructor dice: *'Good morning, team. Last session you read the article. Did anyone find new words in the original Popular Mechanics? (Pause for 2-3 shows of hands.) Great.'* (2 min)

2. Quick pair activity: 'Look at your S2 homework. With your partner — find ONE sentence from the article that tells a tool what to DO. Example: (point to board) Check the floor jack. One sentence each. 90 seconds. Go.' (2 min)
3. 3 volunteers share. Instructor writes examples in red on LIVE ZONE: 'Check the oil.' 'Put on your PPE.' 'Organize the toolbox.' (2 min)
4. Instructor points to sentences: 'What do you notice? The sentences start with a VERB. There is no subject. This is called an IMPERATIVE. That is Grammar Rule 1 — and we'll learn it today.' (1 min)
5. Quick connect to Word Wall: '20 words, still there. We'll use them all when we WRITE today.' (30 seg)

set_up.teacher_talk_opening: *Good morning, everyone! Session 3. Yesterday we READ and learned 20 words. Today we do two things: first, we learn the GRAMMAR — three rules that make sentences work in English in a workshop. Then, we WRITE — a real document, Bay 2 Daily Inspection Checklist and Work Order. This writing is your second evidence — Evidencia 2. So today, we learn the rules AND we use them. Ready?*
set_up.objective: Aprender 3 estructuras gramaticales (Imperatives, There is/are, Prepositions of place). Producir un Daily Inspection Checklist + Work Order completo en inglés (Evidencia 2, 5 pts).
set_up.objective_en_tablero: Today you will: (1) learn 3 grammar rules, (2) practice them in workshop sentences, (3) WRITE a real Checklist + Work Order — EVIDENCE 2.
icq: *How many grammar rules do we learn today?* → Esperan: 3 / Three
*What document will we WRITE today?* → Esperan: Checklist + Work Order / Bay 2 document
*Is the Writing a test or a product?* → Esperan: A product / My document
facilitation_notes: 💡 El warm-up grammar hunt funciona mejor si los aprendices tienen el artículo S2 en mano. Si no lo trajeron: proyectar texto en pantalla brevemente (2 min) y señalar imperativos en rojo.
💡 Anticipa resistencia: 'Grammar = difícil.' Normaliza: 'In English, grammar in the workshop is SIMPLE. Three rules. That's it. You already used them yesterday — you just didn't know the name.'
set_up.checkpoint: ✓ '¿Quién puede decirme el nombre de la primera regla de gramática?' → Esperan: Imperative. Si <50% responde: write IMPERATIVE in large red letters on board and say: 'This is Rule 1. Base verb, no subject. We'll learn it together.' Proceed.

bloques.nombre: Grammar Induction from S2 Text — Discover the Rules
bloques.objetivo: Inducir las 3 estructuras gramaticales target desde el texto S2 usando ejemplos resaltados por color. Producir oraciones propias para cada estructura.
instrucciones_paso_a_paso: PARTE 1 — INDUCCIÓN VISUAL (30 min):
1. Proyectar texto S2 con resaltados de 3 colores ya aplicados:
ROJO = Imperatives: 'Check the floor jack.' / 'Put on your PPE.' / 'Organize the toolbox.'
AZUL = There is/are: 'There is a torque wrench in every bay.' / 'There are 5 tools in a basic kit.'
VERDE = Prepositions: 'The ratchet is in the toolbox.' / 'The jack is next to the bay.'
2. Instructor lee ejemplos en rojo: '¿Qué ven? Starts with a verb. No subject. This is an IMPERATIVE. Rule 1.' Escribe en tablero zona roja.
3. Clase identifica 2 más ejemplos rojos en el texto. Comparte en plenary (2 min).
4. Repetir para AZUL (There is/are): '¿Singular or plural? There IS — one thing. There ARE — more than one.' Escribe en tablero zona azul.
5. Clase identifica 2 más ejemplos azules. Quick test: 'There ___ a spill. (is or are?)' → is. 'There ___ three wrenches. (is or are?)' → are.
6. Repetir para VERDE (Prepositions): 'in, on, next to, behind, near. Where is the tool?' Escribe en tablero zona verde.
7. Clase identifica 2 más ejemplos verdes en texto.
PARTE 2 — PRODUCCIÓN GUIADA EN PARES (25 min):
8. En parejas: completar tabla en worksheet PM-2.10: '3 oraciones en cada color. Use the workshop — the tools and areas you know.' (15 min)
9. Compartir 1 oración por par por color. Instructor escribe en LIVE ZONE. Corrección amable si necesario.
10. Board consolidation: tablero ahora tiene 3+ ejemplos en cada color. 'This is your reference ALL session.'
bloques.teacher_talk_instruction: *Look at the text from yesterday. Do you see the colors? (Point.) RED sentences — these are IMPERATIVES. I'll read them: 'Check the floor jack.' 'Put on your PPE.' What do you notice? (Wait.) Yes — they start with a VERB. No subject — no 'you,' no 'I.' Just the verb. That's an IMPERATIVE. Write this down: RED = IMPERATIVE = verb + rest. (Pause.) Now look at BLUE...*
bloques.teacher_talk_pairs: *Now with your partner: write 3 sentences for each color. Use tools from the Word Wall. ONE red (imperative), ONE blue (there is/are), ONE green (preposition). You have 15 minutes. If you're not sure — look at the board. I'm coming around.*
icq: *For an IMPERATIVE — does it have a subject?* → Esperan: No
*'There IS' — how many things?* → Esperan: One / Singular
*'There ARE' — how many things?* → Esperan: More than one / Plural
*Name one preposition of place.* → Esperan: in / on / next to / behind / near

facilitation_notes: 💡 Inducción > explicación directa: NO explique la regla antes de que los estudiantes la descubran. El color ya hace el trabajo. 'What do you notice?' es la pregunta clave.
💡 El tablero con 3 colores permanece TODA la sesión. Cuando alguien cometa un error en Writing: simplemente señale: 'Look at the board. Which color do you need here?' Sin reexplicar.

💡 'There is/are' es el error más frecuente (confunden singular/plural). Durante la producción en pares, escuche especialmente por 'There are a spill' → corrija señalando: '¿Spill — one or many?' (Pause.) 'One → There IS.'
bloques.checkpoint: ✓ Quick Board Test: Instructor borra las 3 etiquetas de color del tablero. Señala oración: 'Which color is this sentence? Why?' Hace 3 rondas. ≥80% correcto = proceed. <80% = review 2 min: 'Red = action verb first. Blue = There is/are. Green = location word.'
bloques.tecnica_didactica: Inducción gramatical por descubrimiento de colores / Error Log diagnóstico

bloques.objetivo: Identificar y corregir 10 errores frecuentes en las 3 estructuras target en contexto de taller diesel.
instrucciones_paso_a_paso: 1. Distribuir Error Log impreso (10 oraciones con errores de las 3 estructuras).
2. Instrucciones: 'These 10 sentences have errors. FIND the error. CORRECT it. WRITE which rule was broken (Imperative / There is-are / Preposition). You have 20 minutes in pairs.'

3. Modelo rápido: instructor hace oración 1 en voz alta. 'The sentence is: You check the floor jack. Is this correct?' (Wait.) 'No — imperatives don't have a subject. Corrected: Check the floor jack. Rule broken: IMPERATIVE.'
4. Parejas trabajan. Instructor circula, observa errores recurrentes, NO corrige — anota para debrief.
5. Plenary debrief (20 min): instructor lee cada oración. Pregunta: 'What's the error? What's the correction?' Diferentes pares responden.
6. Cada corrección aprobada se escribe en LIVE ZONE del tablero. Al final: 10 oraciones correctas visibles.
7. Quick pattern analysis: '¿Which rule caused the most errors? Why do you think?' (1-2 respuestas.)
bloques.teacher_talk_instruction: *OK. These 10 sentences — there's a problem in each one. Your job: find the problem, correct it, and say which rule is broken. Watch — sentence 1: 'You check the floor jack.' (Pause.) Is this an imperative? (Wait.) No — imperatives don't have 'you.' Corrected: 'Check the floor jack.' Rule broken: IMPERATIVE. (Write on board.) Now — 9 more. With your partner. 20 minutes. Go.*
icq: *For each sentence, how many things do you do?* → Esperan: 3 — find error, correct it, name the rule
*Can you look at the board for the grammar rules?* → Esperan: Yes

error_2.original: There are a spill near Bay 2.
error_2.correction: There is a spill near Bay 2.

error_3.original: The torque wrench is in next to the workbench.
error_3.correction: The torque wrench is next to the workbench.

error_4.error: 'Please' makes it polite request, not imperative; acceptable but not workshop style. Also acceptable as a correction note.

error_5.original: There is three wrenches in the toolbox.
error_5.correction: There are three wrenches in the toolbox.

error_6.original: Put the socket on next to the ratchet.
error_6.correction: Put the socket next to the ratchet.

error_7.original: Checking the floor jack before lifting.
error_7.correction: Check the floor jack before lifting.

error_8.original: There is many hazards in the workshop today.
error_8.correction: There are many hazards in the workshop today.

error_9.original: The fire extinguisher is on next the bay door.
error_9.error: 'on next' — incorrect preposition; should be 'next to'
error_9.correction: The fire extinguisher is next to the bay door.

error_10.original: Organize your tools in the workbench.
error_10.error: 'in the workbench' — tools are ON the workbench, not inside it
error_10.correction: Organize your tools on the workbench.

facilitation_notes: 💡 Errores 4 y 9 son los más matizados. Error 4 ('Please wear') es gramaticalmente aceptable en muchos contextos — guíe la discusión: 'In a workshop, your supervisor says CHECK — not PLEASE CHECK. Directness = professionalism.' Esto conecta con la competencia comunicativa F1.
💡 Si una pareja corrige MAL: no anule. Diga: 'Interesting. Compare with the board — which rule does this sentence need?' Guiar, no anular.

💡 Error 10 (in vs on workbench) es una trampa que distingue niveles. Si alguien lo encuentra sin ayuda: celebrar: 'Excellent — very advanced! The tools rest ON the surface, not inside.' Marca diferencia de nivel.
bloques.checkpoint: ✓ Post-debrief: '¿How many of the 10 did you get right?' Hands up: 10 corrects / 8-9 / 5-7 / below 5. Si >30% got below 5: devote 5 extra min to rules 2 and 3 (most errors). If <10% below 5: proceed normally.
bloques.transition: *Excellent error-hunting. You found 10 problems and fixed them. Now we practice each grammar rule separately — in three stations. Let's move.*
bloques.tecnica_didactica: Estaciones de práctica rotativas (Imperatives / There is-are / Prepositions)

bloques.nombre: Grammar Stations + Safety Report — Focused Practice
bloques.agrupacion: Small groups (3) rotating stations → Individual (Safety Report)
bloques.objetivo: Practicar cada estructura en rotación temática. Producir un Safety Report completo usando obligatoriamente las 3 estructuras.
instrucciones_paso_a_paso: PARTE 1 — GRAMMAR STATIONS (45 min, 3 estaciones x 15 min):
1. Dividir en 3 grupos (2-3 personas cada uno). Asignar estación inicial.
ESTACIÓN 1 — IMPERATIVES (roja):
Tarea: Reescribir 5 instrucciones de seguridad que están en forma incorrecta, convirtiéndolas en imperatives correctos.
Luego: Escribir 3 instrucciones nuevas para Bay 1 que Carlos le daría a Valentina su primer día.
Recursos: Word Wall visible, lista de verbos de acción (check / put / organize / wear / clean / inspect / lift / tighten / fill).
ESTACIÓN 2 — THERE IS/ARE (azul):
Tarea: Describir el workshop layout de S1 (imagen proyectada o impresa). Escribir 8 oraciones: 4 con There IS, 4 con There ARE.
Luego: Leer las oraciones de tu compañero. Verificar: ¿IS o ARE correcto?
Recursos: Workshop layout image, Word Wall.
ESTACIÓN 3 — PREPOSITIONS (verde):
Tarea: Completar mapa del taller con 8 oraciones de ubicación. Cada oración describe DÓNDE está algo.
Luego: Sin mirar el mapa, decirle a tu compañero dónde están 3 herramientas usando solo la oración.
Recursos: Workshop map (S1 image), Word Wall, lista de preposiciones (in/on/next to/behind/near/between).
2. Timer: 15 min por estación. '3 minutes left' warning.
3. Rotar. Continuar hasta completar las 3 estaciones.
PARTE 2 — SAFETY REPORT (15 min):
4. Distribuir formato Safety Report en blanco.

5. Instrucciones: 'Now you write a COMPLETE Safety Report for Bay 2. You MUST use all 3 grammar rules — at least 2 imperatives, 2 There is/are, 2 prepositions. Write 8-10 sentences. You have 10 minutes. Individual work.'
6. Quick share: 2 voluntarios leen su Safety Report. Clase identifica dónde están las 3 estructuras.
bloques.teacher_talk_instruction: *Three stations. Each station focuses on ONE grammar rule. You have 15 minutes per station. At Station 1 (RED) — imperatives. Station 2 (BLUE) — there is/are. Station 3 (GREEN) — prepositions. When the timer rings, ROTATE. Leave your work at the station — the next group reads what you did. Ready? Station 1 — go!*
bloques.teacher_talk_safety_report: *Final part: Now you use ALL THREE rules together — in one Safety Report. It's like what Valentina would write for Carlos. Bay 2. Monday morning. What does she see? What needs to be done? Write 8-10 sentences. MUST include: 2 imperatives, 2 There is/are, 2 prepositions. 10 minutes. Individual. Go.*
icq: *How many minutes at each station?* → Esperan: 15
*After 15 minutes, what do you do?* → Esperan: Rotate
*For the Safety Report — how many grammar rules must you use?* → Esperan: All 3 / Three
*Minimum how many sentences?* → Esperan: 8

station_1_imperatives_corrections: WRONG: You should check the floor jack. → CORRECT: Check the floor jack.
WRONG: Please be organized. → CORRECT: Organize your tools.
WRONG: Wearing PPE is important. → CORRECT: Wear your PPE.
WRONG: The technician cleans the bay. → CORRECT: Clean the bay.
WRONG: It is important to inspect the fire extinguisher. → CORRECT: Inspect the fire extinguisher.

safety_report_sample: Bay 2 Safety Report — Monday 7:00 AM — Technician: Valentina Cruz
1. Check the floor jack. It is ready.
2. There is a small spill near the bay door. Clean the spill immediately.
3. There are three wrenches in the toolbox. They are organized.
4. The fire extinguisher is next to the bay door. It is accessible.
5. Put on your safety goggles before working.
6. There is PPE on the workbench. Use it.
7. The torque wrench is on the shelf. Check its calibration.
8. Inspect the floor jack before lifting any vehicle. Bay 2 is ready.

facilitation_notes: 💡 Estaciones: si solo hay 2-3 estudiantes por estación, la rotación es rápida pero la calidad de práctica es alta. Si hay muchos (>9 aprendices), crear 2 sets de las 3 estaciones.

💡 Safety Report individual: es la transición mental al Writing Task formal (Evidencia 2). Trátelo como práctica, no como evidencia. Tolerancia alta a errores — corrección suave: 'Almost. Which rule do you need here?'
💡 Al final de estaciones: LEAVE WORK at station. El grupo siguiente LEE el trabajo del anterior = doble input. Estudiantes que 'hicieron bien' su estación validan el trabajo del siguiente grupo.
bloques.checkpoint: ✓ Safety Report check: '¿Who used all 3 grammar rules? Raise your hand for imperatives — there is/are — prepositions.' If student can't raise hand for one rule: 'Look at the board. Add one more sentence in that color.' 2 min.
bloques.tecnica_didactica: Análisis de género textual / Escritura modelada co-construida

bloques.nombre: Genre Analysis + Modeled Writing — Document Architecture
bloques.agrupacion: Whole class (genre analysis) → Co-construction with instructor
bloques.objetivo: Analizar estructura, lenguaje y propósito de documentos técnicos reales. Co-construir un Daily Inspection Checklist con el instructor.
instrucciones_paso_a_paso: PARTE 1 — GENRE ANALYSIS (25 min):
1. Proyectar Daily Inspection Checklist real (modelo) + Work Order Header real (modelo).

2. Instructor guía análisis con preguntas: '¿What type of document is this? What is its PURPOSE? Who WRITES it? Who READS it? What LANGUAGE does it use? (Simple? Technical?) ¿What happens if you don't complete it?'
3. En parejas: completar tabla de análisis (en worksheet): Purpose / Writer / Reader / Key vocabulary / Grammar used.

4. Plenary: 3 pares comparten. Instructor sintetiza en tablero: 'A Checklist is FUNCTIONAL. Short sentences. Imperatives for actions. There is/are for conditions. Prepositions for locations. This is EXACTLY what you learned today.'
5. Connect explicitly: '¿Do you see it? These documents USE the 3 grammar rules. This is why we learned them first.'
PARTE 2 — MODELED WRITING (35 min):
6. Instructor toma formato Checklist EN BLANCO en pantalla. 'I'm going to write a Checklist for Bay 1 — THINKING OUT LOUD. You watch, you copy, you question.'
7. Think-aloud writing: instructor escribe en tiempo real, verbalizando decisiones:

'— Item 1: Floor jack. Is it OK or does it need repair? I check. (Pause.) Floor jack — ✓ OK. Now I describe: The floor jack is in position next to Bay 1. (Green = preposition.) I write that as my observation.'
'— Item 2: Spill check. Is there anything on the floor? There is no spill near Bay 1. (Blue = There is.) I write that.'
'— Item 3: Safety instruction for next technician: Check calibration before use. (Red = Imperative.)'
8. Completar 5 items de Checklist en vivo (approx 15 min). Incluir: floor jack, toolbox, PPE, spill check, fire extinguisher.
9. Work Order Header: instructor completa 4 de los 6 campos en vivo: vehicle, bay, technician, maintenance type.
10. '¿Do you see the structure? Now YOU do Bay 2. Same format. Your turn.'
bloques.teacher_talk_instruction: *Look at this document. (Project Checklist model.) This is a REAL Daily Inspection Checklist from a real workshop. Let me ask you — what is this FOR? (Wait.) Yes — to check everything is ready. Who writes it? (The technician.) Who reads it? (The supervisor — Carlos.) What happens if you skip it? (Problems. Safety risks. Legal issues.) Now let's look at the language. Do you see imperatives? There is/are? Prepositions? (Yes!) These three grammar rules — they LIVE in this document. That's why today we learned them first.*
bloques.teacher_talk_modeled: *Now I write — and I think out loud. You copy. You can ask me questions. Watch: (picks up marker) Item 1 — Floor Jack. I go to Bay 1. I check. Floor jack is OK. (Writes: ✓ OK.) Now my observation: (thinking...) The floor jack is... (pause) in position... (pause) NEXT TO Bay 1. I use a preposition. 'The floor jack is next to Bay 1.' (Writes.) ¿Why next to and not in? Because it's beside, not inside. Good. Item 2...*
icq: *Who writes the Checklist?* → Esperan: The technician
*Who reads it?* → Esperan: The supervisor / Carlos
*In the Checklist — which grammar rules do we use?* → Esperan: All 3 / Imperatives + There is/are + Prepositions
*For the Work Order — how many fields must you complete?* → Esperan: 6

genre_analysis_checklist.purpose: To verify that the service bay and all equipment are ready before beginning work
genre_analysis_checklist.key_vocabulary: Toolbelt 20 terms: floor jack, wrench, PPE, fire extinguisher, spill, calibration, etc.
grammar_used: Imperatives for required actions: 'Check calibration before use.'
There is/are for conditions: 'There is no spill in Bay 2.'
Prepositions for locations: 'The fire extinguisher is next to the door.'

genre_analysis_work_order.purpose: To document the maintenance task, assign responsibility, and track completion

modeled_checklist_bay1_sample: 1. Floor jack — ✓ OK | The floor jack is next to Bay 1. Ready to use.
2. Toolbox — ✓ OK | There are 8 tools in the toolbox. All organized.
3. PPE Station — ✓ OK | There are gloves and safety goggles on the shelf.
4. Spill check — ✓ No spill | There is no spill near Bay 1.
5. Fire extinguisher — ✓ OK | The fire extinguisher is next to the bay door. Check pressure monthly.

modeled_work_order_bay1_sample.tools_needed: Torque wrench, ratchet, socket set, floor jack
modeled_work_order_bay1_sample.observations: Vehicle due for oil change. Check calibration of torque wrench before use.

facilitation_notes: 💡 Think-aloud is the PEDAGOGICAL HEART of this bloque. No correr. Verbalizar CADA decisión: '¿Por qué escribo NEXT TO y no IN? Porque el floor jack está al LADO, no adentro.' Esto modela el proceso mental de escribir.

💡 Si alguien pregunta sobre gramática más avanzada (present perfect, etc.): 'Good question — that's S5 and S6. Today, these 3 rules are enough for the document. Keep it simple. Carlos understands simple English perfectly.'
💡 Si termina el Modeled Writing antes de los 35 min: completar el Work Order Header en vivo completo (todos los 6 campos). Más modelo = mejor scaffolding para la escritura individual.
bloques.checkpoint: ✓ 'Before you start writing — show me a thumbs up if you understand the structure. Thumbs sideways if you're not sure. Thumbs down if you're lost.' Count sideways/down. Si >30% no está seguro: 5 min de preguntas y respuestas. Ask: '¿What is the hardest part?' Address that specifically.
bloques.transition: *Good. You've seen how it's done. Now Bay 2 is YOURS. Write your own Checklist and Work Order. This is Evidencia 2 — your evidence of what you can write in English. You have the grammar. You have the vocabulary. You saw the model. Now go.*
bloques.tecnica_didactica: Producción escrita individual / Revisión entre pares (Lista de Verificación No 2)

bloques.nombre: EVIDENCIA 2: Independent Writing Task + Peer Review
bloques.agrupacion: Individual (Writing — 45 min) → Pairs (Peer Review — 20 min) → Plenary (5 min)
bloques.objetivo: Producir individualmente Daily Inspection Checklist + Work Order para Bay 2 (Evidencia 2, 5 pts). Revisar documentos del compañero usando Lista de Verificación No 2.
instrucciones_paso_a_paso: ⚠️ EVIDENCIA 2 — Instrucciones especiales de administración:
PARTE 1 — INDEPENDENT WRITING TASK (45 min):
1. Distribuir: Daily Inspection Checklist en blanco + Work Order Header en blanco (1 de cada uno por aprendiz).

2. Leer escenario en voz alta: 'The Diesel Workshop — Bay 2 — Monday 7:00 AM. You are the technician. You inspect Bay 2 before the first diesel truck of the day. Complete your Checklist AND your Work Order. In English.'

3. Requerimientos (proyectar y leer): 'Checklist: minimum 8 items + at least 2 written observations. Work Order: minimum 6 fields complete. Use the 3 grammar rules (imperatives, there is/are, prepositions). Use Toolbelt vocabulary (minimum 8 terms).'
4. Instructor señala Word Wall y tablero: 'You can use the Word Wall. You can use the board. This is a PRODUCT — not a test from memory. Real technicians use references.'
5. Individual work. Silence preferred but brief questions permitted (vocabulary).
6. Instructor circula, observa. NO corrige durante la escritura — toma notas mentales para feedback posterior.
7. Timer: 45 minutos. '10 minutes left' warning.
PARTE 2 — PEER REVIEW (20 min):
8. Distribuir Lista de Verificación No 2 impresa (10 criterios, 0.5 pt cada uno = 5 pts total).

9. Instrucciones: 'Exchange your documents with your partner. Read their Checklist and Work Order. Use the Lista de Verificación No 2 to evaluate: ¿Does it meet each criterion? ¿Yes or No? Mark it. Then write 2 comments in English: 1 positive, 1 suggestion.'
10. Parejas revisan. Instructor circula, observa calidad del feedback.
11. Quick plenary (5 min): '¿What was the most common STRENGTH you saw? ¿What was the most common thing to improve?' 2-3 respuestas.
12. COLLECT: Instructor recoge AMBOS documentos (original del aprendiz + Lista de Verificación No 2 con peer feedback). Calificación posterior usando Lista de Verificación No 2 como rúbrica formal.
bloques.teacher_talk_instruction: *This is Evidencia 2 — your second formal evidence. (Hold up blank Checklist and Work Order.) Bay 2 is yours. Monday, 7:00 AM. You walk in. What do you see? What needs to be checked? Write it all — in English. (Pause.) You have: the Word Wall, the board, the grammar rules. Use them. Minimum 8 items in the Checklist, minimum 6 fields in the Work Order. Use the 3 grammar rules. You have 45 minutes. This is YOUR document. Write well. Go.*
bloques.teacher_talk_peer_review: *Good work, everyone. Now — peer review. Exchange documents with your partner. (Distribute Lista de Verificación No 2.) Read their Checklist and Work Order. Check each criterion: ¿Yes or No? Then write 2 comments: one thing that is GOOD, one thing they can IMPROVE. Write in English. You have 15 minutes.*

*How many fields in the Work Order?* → Esperan: 6

exemplary_checklist_bay2: Daily Inspection Checklist — Bay 2 — Monday 7:00 AM — Technician: [Student Name]
1. Floor jack — ✓ OK | The floor jack is next to the bay door. No leaks. Ready to use.
2. Toolbox — ✓ OK | There are 6 tools in the toolbox. All organized.
3. Safety goggles — ✓ OK | There are 2 pairs of safety goggles on the workbench.
4. Gloves — ✓ OK | There are 4 pairs of gloves at the PPE station near Bay 2.
5. Fire extinguisher — ✓ OK | The fire extinguisher is next to the bay door. Check pressure.
6. Spill check — ✓ Clear | There is no spill on the floor in Bay 2.
7. Torque wrench — ✓ OK | The torque wrench is in the toolbox. Check calibration before use.
8. Workbench — ✓ Clean | The workbench is organized. All tools are in place.
REQUIRED ACTIONS: Check the floor jack before lifting. Wear your PPE at all times. Inspect the fire extinguisher monthly.

exemplary_work_order_bay2.field_1_vehicle: Diesel truck — Model: Kenworth T680 — Year: 2022
exemplary_work_order_bay2.field_5_tools_needed: Torque wrench, ratchet, socket set, floor jack, work order checklist
exemplary_work_order_bay2.field_6_observations: There is a small spill near the bay entrance. Clean before work begins. The floor jack is ready. Check calibration of torque wrench before tightening bolts.

facilitation_notes: 💡 ⚠️ EVIDENCIA 2 = PRODUCTO INDIVIDUAL. No corregir durante la escritura. Si un estudiante pregunta '¿Cómo se dice X?' → dirigir al Word Wall: 'Look at the wall. Do you see it?' Si no está en el Word Wall: 'Write it in Spanish for now and circle it — I'll help you after.' El objetivo es que PRODUZCAN.

💡 Peer Review es pedagógicamente valioso porque obliga a los aprendices a aplicar los criterios activamente. No simplificar: 'Did they use grammar? Yes/No' es insuficiente. Empujar: '¿WHERE did they use There is/are? Point to it.'
💡 Recoger LA LISTA DE VERIFICACIÓN junto con el documento — la firma del peer reviewer es parte del instrumento de evaluación. Si falta: nota en calificación.
bloques.checkpoint: ✓ 'Before you hand in — check: 8 items in your Checklist? (Count.) 6 fields in your Work Order? (Count.) 2 grammar rules visible? (Point to them.) Good — hand it in.' Esta autochecklist de 30 segundos reduce entregables incompletos.
bloques.tecnica_didactica: Producción escrita individual con revisión entre pares (Lista de Verificación No 2)

breaks.teacher_talk: *OK team — you just corrected 10 grammar errors. Good brain work. Break time — 15 minutes. Stretch. Move. Water. When you come back: Grammar Stations — three tables, three rules, rotation. See you in 15.*

exit_ticket.tarea: Individual (silent, 5 min): Escribe 1 oración para cada regla gramatical: (1) Un imperative para Carlos dándole instrucción a Valentina. (2) Una oración con There is/are describiendo una condición de Bay 2. (3) Una oración con preposición de lugar ubicando una herramienta. Ejemplo: (1) 'Check the torque wrench before tightening.' (2) 'There is a clean floor jack in Bay 2.' (3) 'The fire extinguisher is next to the bay door.'
exit_ticket.success_criteria: ✓ 3 oraciones escritas. ✓ Una por regla (identificable). ✓ Vocabulario del Toolbelt presente.

wrap_up.teacher_talk_closing: *Before we finish — three sentences. One imperative, one there is/are, one preposition. Use workshop vocabulary. You have 5 minutes. Look at the board if you need. Go.* (Wait 5 min.) *Hand it in. Tomorrow — we LISTEN. Carlos and Valentina are talking in Bay 2. You'll hear their conversation — a real safety briefing. After that, YOU will speak. Bring your Voice. See you tomorrow.*

trabajo_autonomo.instrucciones_detalladas: 1. PART 1 (15 min): Review your Peer Review feedback. Read your partner's comments. Do you agree with their suggestions? Revise 2 items in your Checklist based on the feedback. Write the corrected version below the original. 2. PART 2 (15 min): Error practice at home. Write 5 new sentences — ONE for each station: an imperative (Station 1), 2 There is/are sentences (Station 2), 2 preposition sentences (Station 3). Use new situations — not the same ones from class. 3. PART 3 (15 min): Read your S2 article again. This time, underline ALL examples of the 3 grammar targets you can find: imperatives (red), There is/are (blue), prepositions (green). Count them. **Total time: ~45 min (0.75h)**
trabajo_autonomo.entregable: Revised Checklist (2 corrected items) + 5 new grammar sentences + Article re-read with grammar highlights (bring all to S4)
trabajo_autonomo.cuando_se_revisa: S4 SET-UP: Instructor collects grammar sentences, uses for speaking warm-up

wrap_up.preview_next_session: *Next session: LISTENING and SPEAKING. We listen to a real conversation in the workshop — Carlos and Valentina doing a safety briefing. Then you SPEAK — you give your own Workshop Readiness Report to Carlos. 60 to 90 seconds. Like a real technician. Bring your voice.*

answer_key_consolidado.actividad: Bloque A — Grammar Induction: 3 structures identified from text

items.item: Imperatives examples from text

fast_finishers: Bloque A — Induction: If pair finishes color-hunt early: 'Write a FOURTH rule you notice in the text — any other grammar pattern. Be ready to share.' (Open-ended discovery.)

Bloque B — Error Log: If pair corrects all 10 in under 15 min: 'Write 3 NEW sentences with intentional errors — swap with another fast pair and try to find each other's errors.' (Peer-authored Error Log.)
Bloque C — Stations: If group finishes station early: 'Look at the NEXT station's work. Can you add one more sentence to help that group?' (Cross-station scaffolding.)
Bloque E — Evidencia 2: If student finishes Checklist + Work Order in 30 min: 'Write a second Work Order for Bay 1 — for Santiago. Different vehicle, different maintenance type.' (Extended product.)
Peer Review: If finished early: 'Write a THIRD comment — something specific about their grammar use. Which rule did they use best?' (Deeper metalinguistic reflection.)
more_support_needed: Bloque A — Induction: If student can't find color examples: provide pre-highlighted copy of S2 text. Task: 'Just read the red sentences out loud.' Recognition before production.
Bloque B — Error Log: Reduce to 6 sentences (remove 4 most complex: 4, 7, 9, 10). Student corrects 6 and identifies rules. Same cognitive process, lower volume.
Bloque C — Stations: At Station 1, provide verb list (check / put / organize / wear / clean / inspect) as scaffold. At Station 3, provide preposition visual with images (arrow diagrams).

Bloque E — Writing: If student freezes at blank page: '¿Qué ves cuando entras a Bay 2? Di una cosa. Now write that in English. Look at the board and Word Wall.' One item at a time. Do not reduce the total requirement — scaffold the process.

Peer Review: If student can't write comments in English: '¿En español, qué le dirías a tu compañero? Now look at the Word Wall — can you write 3 of those words in English?' Support translation, don't eliminate the task.

instructor_self_check: ¿Todos entregaron Evidencia 2 (Checklist + Work Order + Lista de Verificación No 2)? ¿Hay algún nombre faltante? (Target: 100% entrega. Si alguien faltó: asignar make-up antes de S4.)
¿Los 3 colores del tablero permanecieron visibles toda la sesión? ¿Los aprendices los miraron durante la escritura? (Target: Sí a ambos. Si no: S4 opening — reactivar brevemente los 3 targets.)
¿Qué errores gramaticales vi más durante la escritura individual? (Top 3 patrones: anotar. Usar para micro-repaso en S4 SET-UP o S6 review.)
¿La Evidencia 2 muestra dominio de vocabulario del Toolbelt? ¿O hay aprendices que usaron <5 términos? (Si <5 términos en >30% de documentos: agregar 5 min de vocabulary activation en S4 warm-up.)

¿El tiempo fue suficiente para la escritura individual (45 min)? ¿Algunos terminaron con 15+ min de sobra? (Si sí: próxima vez añadir un segundo documento como extensión. Si muchos no terminaron: ajustar criterio mínimo a 6 ítems en checklist.)
justificacion_didactica: La tarea es producir dos documentos técnicos reales del taller: Daily Inspection Checklist y Work Order. Las actividades de gramática son andamiaje funcional para ejecutar esa tarea de escritura (E2).
